title: Review of c46's hunting predators divide (256^2): Supported. Fresh seeds 14 and 15 give 20 and 14 predator persistent splits (generation 3 and 2), 20 and 22 by the strict test, and one lagged prey-predator swing; most predator daughters fade within ~900 t
summary: Ran the finding's world (defaults; predators added as noise at t=2000) at 256^2 to t=12000 with --lineage-k 5 on seeds 14 and 15. Predators: 35 and 40 splits, 20 and 14 persistent (generation 3 and 2, merge/split 0.11 and 0.18); splits3.py on the predator channel (daughters >= 8 px alive 500 t later): 20 and 22, of which 15 and 14 with no prey within 6 px. Prey: 1 and 2 persistent splits. Counts every 1000 t, seed 14: prey 13/52/56/7/14/48/52/41/31/27/22/19/19, predators 0/0/0/55/62/63/62/49/55/53/37/39/33; seed 15: prey 19/55/61/4/26/49/48/33/27/20/18/27/26, predators 0/0/0/61/61/78/82/64/66/71/64/52/57: prey crash after the predators appear, recover by t~5000-6000 and decline again, one swing. fate.py (predator channel, threshold 0.25): of 69 and 91 daughters of predator splits, 48 and 62 fade below threshold (median life 900 and 800 t), 6 and 17 divide again, 2 and 1 are seen to grow 1.5x.

observations.D: pack256_s14/lineage.png: 20 predator persistent splits, generation 3; pack256_s14/strict_pred.png: rods and Y-shapes pinching into separate droplets at t=2600-11600, 15 of 20 away from prey; seed 15: 14 persistent, generation 2, 22 strict

verdicts.limitation: Predator division is mostly the break-up of a fed, elongated body whose daughters then starve: 48 of 69 and 62 of 91 daughters fade (median 800-900 t) and only 3 of 160 are seen to eat again, so lineages stay at generation 2-3. Prey divide 1-2 times per run. The populations make one lagged swing in 12000 t, not repeated cycles. No predator-free twin in this review (see my review of the ecology claim, seed 13, for one).
